_comment: The answer this fixture exists to pin: which components the traced build
actually used, and why. Hand-authored, deliberately not machine-blessed --
a correctness fixture that regenerates itself from the code under test
proves nothing. Derive each number from trace.jsonl and sbom.cdx.json by
hand before changing it.
zlib            compiles two sources under its root            -> used
json             header-only: named only as an include path    -> used (weaker rung)
vendored-crypto  prebuilt .a, never compiled, only linked -> used (link evidence)
orphan           present in the tree, never compiled           -> UNUSED, and dropped
left-pad         an npm package: no location in the repository -> not judged, kept
The `ar` record that builds libzlib.a produces no evidence by itself --
archiving alone is never proof of use, only of having been built -- and
the /opt/vendor-sdk compile lands outside the scanned root. The final
c++ record links app directly against vendored-crypto's prebuilt .a; that
record has no -c/-S/-E, so it is link-mode, not a compile, and
must not inflate compile_invocations.
product_name / unused_report / discovery_checks used to be hard-coded in
scripts/run_trim_case.py; they moved here so a second trim fixture can
exist. The trim identity is this SBOM's hand-written purl; the scan identity
is what a fresh `scan` of tree/ derives from the folder name. This fixture is
the one that exercises trace DISCOVERY (discovery_checks: true).
